# ROZO payments in Applications

The ROZO product owns its command, browser files, workspace model and Applications adapter. The existing runtime manages Review, Save, Start, Open, Stop and recovery. Its original resource lease covers the selected workspace.

## Open an existing workspace

Initialize the original workspace once, using the installed command:

```sh
starforge rozo-payments init --workspace /absolute/rozo-workspace
```

In Applications, choose **ROZO payments** and select:

| Field | Selection |
| --- | --- |
| Initialized ROZO workspace | The directory containing the original workspace.json and SQLite database. |
| Private connection configuration | The original ROZO connection JSON, with API-key and callback-secret environment references. |
| Private environment JSON | The existing host-local environment file for those references, when required. |
| Local port | 0 chooses an available private loopback port. |

Use the normal Review and Save flow, then Start and Open. The selected native command opens the existing workspace; initialization is a separate explicit native operation. Reopening a workspace preserves its original workspaceId, originId, revisions, saved requests and complete provider observations.

The browser opens the native private session from the launch fragment. Its server authenticates the state request with the same session before Applications retains the URL.

## Source and runtime selection

The source-owned registration is `distribution/contributions/rozo-payments.json`. It contributes the original CLI, package export, runtime manifest, browser asset pair and Applications provider to the normal distribution. The provider is `rozo-payments/application-provider.mjs`.

```sh
starforge registrations --source rozo-payments
starforge registrations --command rozo-payments
starforge doctor --feature rozo-payments
```

Build and install the selected immutable commit through the existing [distribution workflow](../../distribution/CONTRIBUTIONS.md). Its collector reads the same `browser-assets.json` used by the ROZO server. All mapped HTML, JavaScript, CSS and their original imports travel with the selected application.

A selected distribution uses its original `package/manifest.json`, every declared ordinary `package/source` member and the original package.json, README.md and LICENSE. The verifier checks full file lengths and SHA-256 values, the original `packagePath` mapping and all three package hashes. It keeps the complete raw distribution manifest; it does not generate a replacement manifest for the installed package.

A retained standalone checkout can instead select the product's `INSTALLED_SOURCE.json`. That declaration records ordinary repository-relative source paths, byte counts and SHA-256 values while excluding itself. The manifest's raw-file hash is a separate input. Explicit `--source-manifest` and `--source-sha256` selections remain authoritative. Both source forms work with Serve, the native journey and complete workspace export/receiving.

## What the managed launch binds

Review records the initialized workspace directory, immutable workspace marker, private connection configuration, installed source manifest and all selected original source members. Start uses those same inputs and passes the original workspace/origin IDs to the native serve command.

The native source verifier checks the complete manifest. On startup, the adapter also checks the executed release's copy of that selection and reads the original authenticated `/api/state`. The returned workspace IDs and source identity must match the reviewed operation. Mutable workspace work—orders, payment observations, reconciliation editions and corrections—remains in the native workspace.

Private environment values stay in the existing host environment handling. The source manifest, catalog and browser registration carry source paths and metadata. Source imports and receiving retain complete provider records through the native product's original export.

## Operate and receive

Use the native workspace to inspect the original connection aliases, recover saved requests, read payment and callback observations, complete reconciliation and export the full editable receiving package. The product's README describes those business operations and the distinct original merchant and Checkout profiles.

Stopping and continuing use the same saved Applications request and original process lifecycle. Continue reuses the retained argv and workspace identity. Use the existing Applications details and original native logs to inspect the running operation.

For the full shared adapter interface and runtime receiving sequence, see [Applications providers](../../distribution/runtime-workspace/APPLICATION_PROVIDERS.md).

## Complete installed receiving programme

After the original ROZO native operation has completed, run its following installed programme described in [Installed Applications receiving](APPLICATIONS_RECEIVING.md). It builds the selected immutable Git commit, installs the original Node 24 feature without external npm dependencies, operates the same received native workspace through Applications, retains a complete working export and transfers the original runtime. A separate process then installs and receives those same source/workspace bytes.

The fixed programme ID is `ROZO-MERCHANT-SETTLEMENT-COMMISSIONING-20261012:installed-applications`. Its progress, request bodies, accepted replies and complete artifacts remain under the original native directory's `installed-applications` child. Reuse that directory after interruption.

# Complete ROZO receiving

## Choose the intended custody action

A **working export** contains the complete selected source, publisher files, runtime and workspace checkpoint for review. It is received read-only. The source owner can continue normal work after the snapshot.

A **handover** pauses recurring capture, drains in-flight and native work, commits the original seal and packs the complete delivery under the existing operator/native-file leases. It is one normal operator request with one original request ID. The sender stays sealed; only the explicitly received copy can be activated.

Both actions carry:

- Complete application, shared Applications/distribution dependencies, source manifest and original browser assets.
- All selected licensed publisher source and source identity.
- Every explicitly selected Common/decoder dependency runtime file.
- Original workspace/origin marker, SQLite checkpoint, raw response objects and callback bytes.
- Current records, all immutable editions, prepared requests, attempts, responses, source observations, audit and original CLI/native request files.
- Immutable reports and their exact JSON/CSV/HTML bytes in the checkpoint.
- The original private configuration and a relocated receiving template that keeps credential environment-variable names.
- DELIVERY.json with every ordinary member's exact bytes and SHA-256.

Secret environment values are not copied into connection files. The receiving owner supplies credentials through its existing private environment. Callback/raw provider bodies and business records are private delivery content.

## Export or hand over from the original operator

Use the Delivery view while the application owns its original lease. It saves the complete request before dispatch and provides the resulting original archive.

For the standalone CLI, first stop the existing Applications/CLI server so one operator owns the workspace:

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments export \
  --workspace /private/merchant/rozo \
  --config /private/merchant/rozo-connections.json \
  --id merchant-review-001 --request-id export:merchant-review-001 \
  --revision ACTUAL_REVISION --actor "Original operator" \
  --title "Merchant settlement review"
~~~

The explicit custody transfer is:

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments handover \
  --workspace /private/merchant/rozo \
  --config /private/merchant/rozo-connections.json \
  --id merchant-handover-001 --request-id handover:merchant-001 \
  --revision ACTUAL_REVISION --actor "Original operator" \
  --title "Complete merchant operations handover"
~~~

When source is run from a retained checkout, supply --source-root, --source-manifest and optionally --source-sha256. For a standalone checkout, source-root is the repository root and the manifest is the product's INSTALLED_SOURCE.json. Installed packages automatically select their original distribution manifest beside package/source; an explicit source-manifest remains authoritative. Use --python or ROZO_PYTHON when the host's Python executable is not named python3.

The resulting delivery descriptor includes deliveryId, workspaceId, originId, revision, mode, original requestId, archive bytes/SHA-256, manifest SHA-256, name and local path. The native files are:

~~~text
<workspace>/deliveries/<deliveryId>/Rozo_Workspace.zip
<workspace>/deliveries/<deliveryId>/EXPORT.json
<workspace>/deliveries/<deliveryId>/contents/DELIVERY.json
~~~

Download through the original archive button or retain those completed files with their exact hashes.

## Interrupted export and handover

The original seal can be accepted before archive assembly finishes. An error at that point is a pending delivery, not permission to open a new owner or issue another handover. The original request, source manifest and configuration bytes remain its binding.

Resume the same request:

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments resume --workspace /private/merchant/rozo \
  --config /private/merchant/rozo-connections.json \
  --request-id handover:merchant-001
~~~

Resume retains completed members and the original checkpoint. A different pre-existing member or changed source/configuration stops with an explicit conflict. Restore the original bound source/configuration before continuing; never edit accepted delivery members to make their hashes fit. A subsequent working snapshot is a new explicit export, while the prior accepted snapshot remains retained.

## Receive the exact archive

Review mode:

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments receive \
  --archive /private/incoming/Rozo_Workspace.zip \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --directory /private/received/merchant-001
~~~

Receiving rejects traversal paths, symlinks, duplicate or unlisted archive members, missing members and changed file hashes. It verifies the complete source declaration and original SQLite workspace/export request. The result returns actual sourceRoot, sourceManifest, workspaceDirectory, configuration and cli paths. The source-manifest path identifies the raw original declaration selected by this archive.

The complete extracted layout is:

~~~text
DELIVERY.json
RECEIVED_ARCHIVE.json
source/<original repository-relative application paths>
source-package/manifest.json       # installed distributions
source-package/package.json       # original package metadata
source-package/README.md
source-package/LICENSE
workspace/workspace.json
workspace/RECEIVING.json
workspace/rozo.sqlite3
workspace/cli-requests/...
workspace/native/...
configuration/original.json
configuration/received-template.json
configuration/connections.json
publishers/<original alias>/...
runtimes/<original alias>/...
~~~

Working copies are protected by the receiving marker even if a copied old lease appears free. Read the received state using the returned CLI and workspace paths; do not initialize or manufacture a new workspace over it.

## Activate a sealed handover

Only mode handover supports activation:

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments receive \
  --archive /private/incoming/Rozo_Workspace.zip \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --directory /private/received/merchant-001 \
  --activate --request-id receive:merchant-001 --actor "Receiving operator"
~~~

This verifies the original seal, records an immutable receiving action with the archive/manifest identity, retains the copied original lease rows in custody, clears only those copied leases and creates the received active-control edition. Workspace ID, origin ID, original business records and original request histories are preserved. The revision advances by the single explicit receiving action. Repeating the same activation returns its original accepted result.

Start the returned CLI with the returned workspace/configuration. Supply the same credential environment-variable names through the receiving host's existing private environment. The old sender remains sealed.

## Maintained native operation

Run the product's exact full native receiving command:

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments native \
  --directory /private/rozo-native/original-operation \
  --source-root /original/repository \
  --source-manifest /original/repository/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/INSTALLED_SOURCE.json \
  --chromium /actual/installed/chromium \
  --playwright-module /actual/installed/playwright/index.mjs \
  --python /actual/python3
~~~

The fixed operation is ROZO-MERCHANT-SETTLEMENT-COMMISSIONING-20261012. Always reuse its saved directory after interruption. Native progress retains the original workspace, every request body, source editions and each completed phase. An unavailable browser produces a pending result before working export/handover; supply the actual browser runtime and continue that same directory.

The native flow performs:

1. Receive all original Checkout source; create original profiles/orders in the owned development workspace.
2. Accept a keyed create in the local merchant fixture, lose its response, and recover by original app/order lookup without another create.
3. Capture 106 payments through complete pagination, including failed/expired/refunded states.
4. Receive signed, duplicate, older and conflicting callback bodies while preserving raw bytes and stage meanings.
5. Save source-based correction/fulfilment and immutable reports, compare them and verify every original report file.
6. Exercise recurring catch-up and pause it through original requests.
7. Invoke the actual Checkout publisher quote/create/status/resume code. Recover the deliberately lost create response using actual original invoice/payment IDs.
8. Operate all seven staff views in one real browser context, edit through the actual form, lose the accepted response, reload and recover the same request, inspect history, download originals and capture desktop/mobile views.
9. Export and receive a complete working snapshot, proving it cannot become a writable owner.
10. Drain/seal/export the original handover, close its operator and execute receiving from the extracted application in a separate Node process.
11. Compare all original records, editions, requests, attempts, raw objects, observations, callbacks and audit rows across receiving; permit only the single explicit activation additions.

The fixture is labelled DEVELOPMENT. It preserves original publisher fixture bytes and records the explicit local timestamp/expiry derivations. It makes no real provider payment or signed transaction. Common SDK live operations and deployed Stellar RPC decoding remain separate configured profiles whose actual execution requires their selected native runtimes and account/deployment inputs.

## Completion and portable continuation

The operation writes NATIVE_PROGRESS.json, exact browser progress/downloads/screenshots, RECEIVING_PROCESS.json and NATIVE_COMPLETION.json. The received application writes NATIVE_RECEIVE_RESULT.json and its accepted activation. Source editions, provider fixture and full workspace remain alongside the original operation.

Only NATIVE_COMPLETION.json with all phases and actual separate receiving result is complete. A prepared source packet, grammar pass or pending browser state is a different milestone.

Move a stopped operation as a whole when changing equipped hosts: retain all files and empty directories, original source editions, provider fixture state, SQLite state, native/CLI requests and progress. Preserve original endpoint/case bindings and reconcile the actual old process/lease before continuing. Local and equipped receivers run this same source and operation; do not start a competing job.

## Receive an installed Applications package

[Installed Applications receiving](APPLICATIONS_RECEIVING.md) is the complete following programme for the already completed native case. The original distribution builder and runtime-transfer installer keep their own source/profile/lock identities. A working export from the installed ROZO listener keeps that exact distribution manifest and its three package files, alongside every declared source member and the original workspace. The archive receiver remains manifest-driven; it verifies all declared metadata instead of substituting the standalone source declaration.

The independent `applications-receiving.mjs` process runs from the transferred runtime's own source. It verifies the full original runtime transfer, completes the original installer, receives the exact working archive and compares every native table and raw object with the accepted export inventory. The working copy remains read-only. Permanent custody transfer continues to use the explicit Handover operation above.

# Complete installed Applications receiving

This is the following installed programme for the already completed original ROZO merchant/Checkout case. It uses the original distribution builder, runtime installer, Applications owner and runtime-transfer receiver. The existing native payment/source journey remains the commissioning record.

## Select the original operation and published source

The initial native operation must already have its complete `NATIVE_COMPLETION.json`, original sender, active received workspace, original configuration template and retained native artifacts. The installed programme opens `<native-directory>/received/workspace`; it does not initialize another ROZO case or replay the earlier merchant/Checkout requests.

Select the complete published Git commit containing this programme and the original ROZO source-owned contribution. Use an existing checkout with that commit available in its object database.

~~~sh
starforge rozo-payments native-applications \
  --directory /private/rozo-native/original-operation \
  --repository /original/merchant-workspace-checkout \
  --ref COMPLETE_40_CHARACTER_COMMIT \
  --chromium /actual/installed/chromium \
  --playwright-module /actual/installed/playwright/index.mjs \
  --python /actual/python3 \
  --npm /actual/npm
~~~

The command requires Node 24 or later, Python 3, the original `flock` host command, npm and the already available Playwright/Chromium runtime. The selected ROZO feature has no external npm dependencies. The original installer still packs, installs and verifies its exact empty dependency profile and lockfile. Browser tools are receiving-host inputs and are not invented application dependencies.

The fixed programme ID is:

~~~text
ROZO-MERCHANT-SETTLEMENT-COMMISSIONING-20261012:installed-applications
~~~

It owns only the original native directory's `installed-applications` child and its original kernel lease. Keep the entire native directory and this child together after interruption. The retained binding includes the native completion hash, original workspace/origin IDs, selected Git commit, actual checkout and original executable selections. Restore those paths and original files before continuation on another equipped host.

## What the programme completes

| Phase | Original action and retained result |
| --- | --- |
| Native input | Open the original active received workspace and retain every table/object identity. |
| Build | Call the original `buildDistribution` with selection `rozo-payments`, the exact commit, offline source and resumable output. |
| Install | Prepare/install the original `native:false`, `features:['rozo-payments']`, `operator:true` profile. Require Node 24, zero external dependencies, READY state, exact source and lock. |
| Review and Save | Attach that READY runtime to one original Applications workspace, submit the actual Review and Save HTTP actions, and retain the complete original bodies, UUIDs and replies. |
| Connect and Start | Reuse the saved application's original managed runtime adoption, Review Start and Start. Require the actual running listener, original application/run identity and authenticated workspace/source state. |
| Browser | Select the saved application in the real Applications library, use its actual Open control, inspect the same ROZO workspace and retain desktop/narrow screenshots. |
| Working export | Submit one exact native `workspace.export` request to the installed listener, receive the complete original ZIP download and retain every native row/object identity. Earlier native rows must remain unchanged. |
| Stop | Use the real Stop control when its browser is present; otherwise reconcile the already retained exact Stop request through the same original API. Wait until that run is inactive and its original worker lease is free. |
| Runtime transfer | Export the original runtime's source/profile/lock package, retain every declared part, and receive all parts through the original transfer APIs. |
| Independent receiving | Launch a separate Node process from the transferred runtime's own `applications-receiving.mjs`. Complete the original installer and receive the same working archive from its extracted source. |
| Completion | Compare complete native tables/raw objects, preserve the read-only working-copy marker and retain the full application history, source/runtime identities and all artifact hashes. |

The full native fixture remains DEVELOPMENT. The installed programme makes no provider payment and signs no transaction; the original fixture's recurring schedule is paused. Its only ROZO business-workspace append is the explicit working-export request and delivery record. The original handover sender remains sealed, and the original active receiver remains the selected workspace.

## Exact source identity

A selected built package retains the original `stellar-forge.merchant-distribution-manifest.v1` bytes. Each original source row must keep its `path`, `packagePath: 'source/' + path`, byte count and SHA-256. The original package.json, README.md and LICENSE are retained with their declared hashes. Package name/version must match the original manifest.

Source inspection accepts that built package or the complete standalone `INSTALLED_SOURCE.json`. Applications prepare/start and the native CLI select the same actual source form. The executed installed programme's own full source hash must equal its row in the selected published package.

An installed working export retains:

~~~text
DELIVERY.json
source/<every declared repository-relative source member>
source-package/manifest.json
source-package/package.json
source-package/README.md
source-package/LICENSE
workspace/<original full checkpoint and request/source files>
configuration/original.json
configuration/received-template.json
publishers/<selected original publisher files>
runtimes/<selected original dependency files>
~~~

The source-package metadata travels with the archive. A receiver does not rewrite the distribution manifest to resemble a standalone checkout.

## Continue a lost response or interrupted host

Run the same command with the same original directory and source binding. Progress retains exact request bodies before dispatch and preserves accepted result files before advancing its phase.

- Save reuses the original UUID and review ID. An earlier retained success plus a missing native application stops for original-store restoration.
- Start uses its original UUID, complete reviewed argv and resource selection. A prepared run without a dispatched worker resumes through the original Applications recovery API.
- An active original worker is reused. The programme never infers that an inaccessible process has stopped.
- A definitively drained listener can receive an explicitly recorded following start after its original worker lease is free. EXITED, LAUNCH_FAILED or reconciled terminated-process outcomes qualify only when no Stop was requested. Every earlier run and request stays in history. An unknown launch outcome or an explicit Stop requires the original operator reconciliation.
- The original working-export request is retained before its first POST. A lost response retries that same body; the native service checks its original fingerprint and returns or finishes the accepted delivery.
- Stop keeps the original application/run IDs. The programme waits for the same worker to drain before runtime receiving.
- An interrupted runtime preparation preserves its complete partial directory. The original `recoverRuntime` or runtime-transfer recovery composes a new target from those retained originals. A missing previously accepted READY runtime requires restoration.
- An existing complete receiving result is compared with the original selection and reused. It is never replaced with a fresh result merely because the caller lost its response.

The original Applications workspace is part of the operation. Restore its native state and history rather than replacing it with a new empty workspace. Progress or local request files that retain full exact bytes can restore missing redundant receipt copies; a missing authoritative native store is a different condition.

## Native source entry points

| Source | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `native-applications.mjs` | Full original build/install/Applications/export/transfer continuation and durable phase/request journal. |
| `applications-browser.mjs` | Actual saved application selection, Open, native state read, Stop control and screenshots. |
| `applications-receiving.mjs` | Independent process from received source; exact runtime installation and read-only working archive receiving. |
| `source.mjs` | Original distribution or standalone manifest inspection, complete package metadata and explicit source selection. |
| `delivery.mjs` | Full native workspace export/receive and exact original source-package retention. |
| `application-provider.mjs` | Original Applications source-owned prepare/startup binding. |

`applications-receiving.mjs --selection FILE` consumes the exact selection written by the parent programme. It is not a new workspace initializer. The selection binds the original native completion, application and run, complete transfer manifest, original runtime, working archive/hash, full export inventory and request ID. Keep that file unchanged.

## Complete output and acceptance

The output child contains:

~~~text
PROGRESS.json
requests/<full original HTTP and receiver request files>
http-receipts/<complete original responses>
receipts/<completed phase results>
source-package/<original selected source archive and build state>
runtime-N/<original installed runtime and source/profile/lock>
staff-workspace-N/<Applications records, managed homes, runs and history>
browser/<original run UUID>/<desktop, narrow and stopped screenshots>
Rozo_Installed_Workspace.zip
EXPORTED_WORKSPACE_INVENTORY.json
runtime-transfer/<original export manifest, source/profile/lock and parts>
runtime-transfer-received/<complete original receiving state>
received-runtime-N/<original transferred runtime installation>
received-working-workspace/<complete read-only working archive>
receiving-stdout.log
receiving-stderr.log
INSTALLED_RECEIVING_RESULT.json
APPLICATIONS_COMPLETION.json
~~~

Only `APPLICATIONS_COMPLETION.json` with the accepted independent receiver, exact archive/runtime/source identities, actual original application/run and complete artifact hashes is installed completion. A source publication, READY runtime, accepted Start or pending browser is a retained intermediate result. The original `NATIVE_COMPLETION.json` remains unchanged.

Keep the complete operation for further customer receiving, including private configuration/response bytes and its original request history. Ordinary working snapshots remain useful during operation. Permanent custody transfer is still the explicit native Handover action described in [Complete ROZO receiving](RECEIVING.md).
